newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends mostly down on pessimism.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends mostly down on pessimism.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended mostly down on Friday on pessimistic sentiment about the short-term outlook after London Metal Exchange (LME) prices were unable to clear $2,415 overnight, traders said.
The LME's subsequent slippage under $2,400 suggested seven-week lows of $2,355 hit on Wednesday could come under attack again, they said.

In Shanghai, the most actively traded October 1997 contract ended at 22,160 yuan ($2,673) per tonne, losing 90 yuan. It opened at 22,230 yuan, hitting an intraday high of 22,280 and a low of 22,060 yuan per tonne.
July was unchanged at 21,750, August fell 70 yuan to 21,930, September 170 to 22,080, November 150 to 22,150 and December rose 110 to 22,210 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume fell to 49,710 tonnes from 88,950 tonnes.
Copper opened lower, though at the intraday high for most contracts, and fell further for most of the session.
Traders said market sentiment was pessimistic sentiment, with investors unwilling to build long positions at current levels.
"Investors believe copper will fall further, which brought heavy selling pressure at higher levels," one trader said.
"The slight rebound on the LME overnight, coupled with the oversold technical charts, was not enough to improve confidence among long position holders," he said.
The price of physical copper had fallen to around 21,800 to 22,000 yuan per tonne, against Thursday's 22,100 to 22,300 yuan, on good local supply, traders said.
After the dips of recent days, the local red metal was unlikely to fall sharply in the short term unless there was some major negative news, they said.
Traders said they expected copper to meet strong support at the 22,000-yuan level in the short term.
Aluminium ended mixed. July fell 10 yuan to 13,590, August 20 to 13,780, September rose 70 to 13,950 and October 190 to 14,050 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume rose to 3,310 tonnes from 2,260 tonnes.
